text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government wants to amend public funds protection law.
- Kuwait's Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan flies to Syria to hold talks with Syrian officials on boosting economic cooperation.
- Eighty firms to take part in Kuwait food-producers fair.
- Finance Ministry wants more non-oil revenue in 1997-98 state budget, officials say.

- Constitutional court sets December 29 to look into a request by parliament to examine the speaker's election procedures. MP Jassem al-Kharafi, a former finance minister, said the October election of opposition vetran Ahmad al-Saadoun as speaker did not meet constitutional rules.
- Gulf Bank set to make $100.3 million net profit in 1996.
- Kuwait Investment Authority, the state investment arm, studies the feasibility of privatising public transport company.
- Trade Ministry uncovers large-scale commercial fraud in consumer goods.
